missionPremise: OPS-23 finding (plan section 2, and the wave-1 verify record _inbox/2026-09-11_ops23_wave1_verify_p157.md): Travis (48453) cad_property rows carry present market/land/improvement values but null living_area_sqft and year_built, and both the factory writer (ingest-existing.js applyCadScalar/stampAbsent) and cortex (structuralFactResolve.ts) stamp that null as absent-verified, which asserts a detail file was consulted and found nothing. ENFORCEMENT.md: converting unaccounted to absent-verified when nothing looked is a lie that passes every check. The named fix is to load the improvement-detail file the roll export omits and re-run the fill so genuinely-present rows move from absent-verified/unaccounted to present, honestly narrowing the set that stays absent-verified.
completionPredicate: Property Explorer facets (and get_smart_site) show structuralFact.state present with non-null livingAreaSqft and yearBuilt for BOTH 48453:113408 and 48453:474034, AND the county-wide null count on improved cad_property rows (improvement_value > 0) measurably falls between a before and after county-rail-coverage-report reading. Per the mission's own pre-registered falsifier, anything short of both legs is not done regardless of what any job reports.
scopeBasis: Mission and OPS-23 program law both restrict this lane to: (1) acquiring the public detail file, (2) loading it through the cloud loader (never a laptop), (3) running the existing fill job, (4) measuring with the existing/triggered coverage instrument, (5) confirming the served surface, explicitly forbidding writer-rule changes, filename renames, regex widening, entitlement/pricing changes, and factory data runs before the planner serialises P-157 against P-158. Two independent findings below (no cloud loader exists for this ingest path; the live export's filenames do not match the code's discovery pattern) each independently trigger the mission's own explicit clause: 'If the cloud loader cannot take the second file, STOP at CP1 and report the gap; do not run from a laptop and do not widen the freeze.' Renaming files or widening the discoverFiles regex to route around the mismatch is also explicitly out of scope per OPS-23's program-wide rule ('Do not fix a naming mismatch by renaming; report it.'). That leaves nothing in this lane's authority to execute past design/investigation, so CP1 is where this lane stops pending the planner/overseer's ruling.

falsifierPreRegistered.primary: If after a fill, structuralFact is not present with a living area and a year built for BOTH 48453:113408 and 48453:474034 on the Property Explorer facets, the row is not done; and if the county-wide null count on improved parcels does not fall between the before and after readings, nothing was loaded, whatever the job said.
falsifierPreRegistered.secondMechanismConsidered: A load could succeed at the database layer and the panel could still look unchanged for three independent reasons, each checked separately rather than assumed away: (1) baked facets -- the probe fixtures show bakedAt 2026-07-24/2026-09-10 for these parcels' snapshots, so a DB-only fill would not move the served facet until the existing LDT bake path re-runs for these parcel ids; the close must name that bake invocation explicitly, never hand-edit the served value. (2) an overlay reading a different rail -- routes/propertyExplorer.ts:298-301 overlays parcel_record's own livingAreaSqft on top of the cortex cad_property read via cadRollFactFromParcelRecord.ts; a fill that only updates the factory's parcel_record_cell without cad_property itself getting the value (or vice versa) can leave one of the two paths stale while the other reports present -- both must be checked, not just structuralFactResolve.ts's cad_property source. (3) a cache -- parcelRecordReaderClient.ts (landed today in commit 55c4ad4, per the LDT snapshot drift above) added a 'coalescing, short-TTL cache' in front of the new one-reader HTTP path; this is now live on origin/main at the LDT start commit and was not in the mission's verify snapshot. It is a short-TTL cache per its own PR description, so it is unlikely to explain a stale read taken minutes apart, but a close that shows unchanged facets immediately after a load must re-probe after the TTL window before concluding the load failed, not before.
falsifierPreRegistered.verifiedAtThisCheckpoint: Live get_smart_site (depth=node) run 2026-09-11 for both probe parcels confirms the mission's premise exactly, not just the code trail: 48453:113408 and 48453:474034 both currently show structuralFact.status absent, verdict absent-verified, basis 'CAD row present but structural fields (living_area_sqft, year_built) are null', scopeSearched 'cad_property tax_year=2026 tier=cad-export'. onRecord.cadRoll shows improvementValue/marketValue/landValue/assessedValue all present with source cad_property for both parcels -- consistent with the roll's base PROP.TXT-equivalent having loaded fine and only the improvement-detail-derived fields being null. This is today's actual 'before' baseline for the falsifier, not an assumption.

findings.title: No cloud-hosted execution path exists for lib/cad-ingest at all -- not merely one that cannot take a second file
evidence: gcloud run jobs list --project hauska-prod-497015 --region us-east4 (the region the 2026-08-26 cloud-loader design uses, live-queried 2026-09-11): 36 jobs, all named factory-<jobname>, every one a hauska-factory src/jobs/*.mjs script (factory-parcel-record-fill, factory-atoms-cad, factory-f10-cad-loop, factory-landing-import, etc). None wraps legacy-design-tools' lib/cad-ingest.
gcloud run jobs list --region us-central1: empty (only long-running Services, not Jobs, run there).

legacy-design-tools has no Dockerfile, cloudbuild*.yaml, or CI deploy step anywhere under lib/cad-ingest/; its own package.json defines only a local script: "cad-ingest": "tsx src/cli.ts" (lib/cad-ingest/package.json:17), invoked per its own usage header as `pnpm --filter @workspace/cad-ingest cad-ingest -- --county=... --file=...`, reading a plain DATABASE_URL env var (cli.ts:254-256) with no staging/production target selector of the kind hauska-factory's own publish-target-env.mjs implements for its bakes.

sources.ts's own documented usage for the sibling PACS county Hays (48209, manual-download like Travis) instructs a human to download the ZIP and run the CLI locally -- confirming this tool's designed operating mode is local, not cloud.
findings.conclusion: The 2026-08-26 ingest-freeze decision's 'Cloud Run Job' re-engineering is scoped to the atoms-county-loader (the atoms/atom_links tables, hauska-engine's write-*-county.mjs scripts) -- a different pipeline, different repo, different store than cad_property. That decision never mentions lib/cad-ingest or cad_property. The mission's step 2 premise ('the load runs where that decision says loads run... If the cloud loader cannot take the second file, STOP') presupposes a cloud loader for this specific path exists and just might be missing one feature; the actual gap is one level up -- there is no cloud loader for this path to be missing a feature from. This triggers the mission's stop clause a fortiori.

findings.title: The live Travis 2026 certified export's internal filenames do not match cad-ingest's PACS file-discovery pattern -- a naming mismatch, not a data-format incompatibility
evidence: cli.ts discoverFiles for format=pacs (cli.ts:123-135): requires a filename matching /APPRAISAL_INFO\.TXT$/i, optionally /APPRAISAL_IMPROVEMENT_DETAIL\.TXT$/i.

Public record, no credential: fetched https://traviscad.org/publicinformation/ (2026-09-11), found and confirmed via HTTP HEAD the current '2026 Certified Appraisal Export Supp 0_07182026.zip' (Content-Length 557,228,168 bytes) at https://traviscad.org/wp-content/largefiles/2026%20Certified%20Appraisal%20Export%20Supp%200_07182026.zip.

Read only the zip's central directory via an HTTP Range request for the trailing ~3MB (no full download) and listed its 21 entries: PROP.TXT (4,895,747,376 B), IMP_INFO.TXT (52,778,376 B), IMP_DET.TXT (2,065,539,840 B), LAND_DET.TXT, IMP_ATR.TXT, APPR_HDR.TXT, etc -- an entirely different naming convention (True Automation/PACS 'legacy 8.0.33' layout per the page's own 'Website_Legacy8.0.33-AppraisalExportLayout' export-layout file) than /APPRAISAL_INFO\.TXT$/ or /APPRAISAL_IMPROVEMENT_DETAIL\.TXT$/. None of the 21 entries match either regex.

Fetched IMP_DET.TXT's local-header byte range directly (a second targeted Range request, ~300KB, no full download) and decompressed a live sample. The fixed-width byte spans layout.ts declares (propId 1-12, propValYr 13-16, typeCd 41-50, typeDesc 51-75, yrBuilt 86-89, area 94-108) were sliced against the real decoded record and align exactly: propId '000000100008', propValYr '2026', typeCd '551', typeDesc 'PAVED AREA' (trimmed), yrBuilt '1984', area '00017100.000000'. CRLF-terminated fixed-width records, as the parser expects.

grep across lib/cad-ingest for IMP_DET, IMP_INFO, PROP.TXT, LAND_DET, or any Travis-specific rename/alias table: no matches. No mechanism in the code maps these literal Travis filenames onto the roles discoverFiles looks for.
findings.conclusion: The byte layout is correct for this file; only the outer filename fails the match. Historically-loaded cad_property values for Travis (present improvementValue/marketValue/landValue, confirmed live above) mean some earlier load succeeded despite this -- most plausibly via an undocumented manual rename before invoking the CLI, consistent with the wave-1 verify doc's finding that 'whether the Travis load ever carried the detail file is recorded nowhere in either repo.' OPS-23's program law is explicit: 'Do not fix a naming mismatch by renaming; report it. Do not widen a check to admit a value it does not satisfy; report it.' Both apply here verbatim. This finding is reported, not fixed, and stands independently of F-CP1-1 -- even if a cloud execution surface existed today, feeding it this real export as-is would still fail discoverFiles.

findings.title: The roll vintage has moved since the original Travis load; which base file to pair with the improvement-detail file is undecided
evidence: Live get_smart_site output for both probe parcels stamps ownerFact/landUseFact sourceVintage as the URL-decoded string '2026 preliminary appraisal export supp 0_07072026' -- an earlier, 'preliminary' vintage than the currently published '2026 Certified Appraisal Export Supp 0_07182026.zip'.
findings.conclusion: Per R-1 (most-current source wins) the certified 07182026 export is the fresher, more authoritative roll, but re-loading against it would also refresh market/land/improvement values already marked present from the preliminary roll -- a wider change than 'add the missing structural fields' and not something this lane should decide unilaterally. Flagged for the overseer/planner: pair the improvement-detail file with a repeat of the original preliminary roll (narrowest change, only fills the two null fields) or adopt the current certified roll wholesale (larger, R-1-consistent change). Not decided here.

designForStep4Instrument.summary: Not yet implemented -- design only, per 'before any code' at CP1. Add a branch to hauska-factory src/cli.mjs following the file's existing pattern (dynamic import + JSON.stringify(out) + return), e.g. `if (cmd === "county-rail-coverage-report") { const { parseCoverageReportFlags, runCountyRailCoverageReport } = await import("./jobs/county-rail-coverage-report.mjs"); const flags = parseCoverageReportFlags(process.argv.slice(3)); const out = await runCountyRailCoverageReport(process.env, { flags }); console.log(JSON.stringify(out)); return; }` -- no change to the job module itself, which is already read-only and correctly shaped.
